newsitem.title: CHINA: Yizheng says China govt studying merger.
newsitem.headline: Yizheng says China govt studying merger.

text.p: Yizheng Chemical Fibre Co Ltd said on Monday that government administrative officials were studying the possibility of a merger, but it had not received any formal notification of merger plans.

In a company statement in the Shanghai Securities News, Yizheng said that as the possibility of a merger was being studied at higher levels, it was not appropriate for the company to make any comment.
An announcement would be made at the appropriate time, it said.
The company had asked the Hong Kong stock exchange to resume trading of its H shares from 10:00 a.m. (0200 GMT) on Monday, the statement said.
Trading in Yizheng's H shares was suspended on July 31 at the company's request.
Trading in Yizheng's domestic currency A shares on the Shanghai stock exchange would be suspended on Monday morning and resume in the afternoon, the Shanghai Securities News said.
Yizheng, based in Jiangsu province, is one of the world's biggest polyester manufacturers.
Its share price surged last week on rumours that it would merge with the Yangzi Petrochemical Corp, Yizheng's main raw material supplier.
Yizheng's last traded price on July 31 was HK$2.625.
